encounters.title: The Overturned Postal Van
encounters.description: An overturned postal van on the ring road, the driver long dead at the wheel. The back is burst open: undelivered letters scattered by the wind, a few supply packs still strapped in, and one sealed envelope addressed to someone at the nearest settlement, the name written in a careful hand.

choices.text: Read the undelivered letters where they lie
Carry the sealed envelope to its addressee
Take the supply packs and leave the post
Burn the van to stop the wind scattering the letters

encounters.title: The Still Weather Station
encounters.description: A automated weather station, solar panel still charging, instruments still logging to a dead network. The data is days old. A tarp has been stretched under the panel — someone sheltered here recently and left a tin cup, clean, upside down.

choices.text: Extract the weather data from the logger
Take the solar panel for the shelter
Scavenge the instruments and leave the station dead
Leave it running and take only the tin cup

encounters.title: The Pianist
encounters.description: In a ruined concert hall, a man plays an upright piano with three working keys. He does not stop when you enter. He plays the same three-note phrase, over and over, as if waiting for the fourth. The hall is cold. He is thin. He has been here a long time.

choices.text: Sit and listen until he finishes (he does not finish)
Share what food you have and wait for the fourth note
Tell him about the shelter and offer to guide him back
Destroy the piano so he will come with you

encounters.title: The Roadside Trader
encounters.description: A woman with a cart on the highway, pulled to the shoulder. She has salt, two tins, and a working flashlight. She wants medical supplies, which you have. She does not want to know your name and does not offer hers. She counts by touch, not by sight.

choices.text: Trade the medical supplies for the salt and tins
Trade only for the flashlight, keep the medical
Trade everything she asks for everything she has
Refuse and leave her to the road

encounters.title: The Water Seller
encounters.description: At a crossroads, a man selling filtered water by the cup. His filter is real — you can see the charcoal and sand. His price is information: he wants to know which settlements are still occupied. He will trade water for names.

choices.text: Give him the names of the settlements you know
Drink one cup and give him nothing
Offer to trade for his filter, not his water
Walk away — water for names is a bad trade

encounters.title: The False Broadcast
encounters.description: A working radio on a counter, tuned to a frequency that is broadcasting a settlement's location and an invitation: 'Come, we have food and medicine, we are at the old school, we are many.' The broadcast is clear. The broadcast is too clear. The frequency is one that was silent a week ago.

choices.text: Go to the school to verify the broadcast
Rebroadcast a warning that the signal may be a trap
Destroy the radio so no one else hears it
Ignore it and continue — it is not your frequency

encounters.title: The Two Camps
encounters.description: Two camps, visible across a valley, both flying the same rag flag. One has smoke (cooking). One does not. A figure on the ridge tells you the smoking camp is raiders using the flag as bait; the smoking camp's own scout told you yesterday the ridge camp is the raider. Both cannot be telling the truth. Both could be.

choices.text: Trust the ridge figure and approach the cold camp
Trust the smoke and approach the cooking camp
Avoid both camps and take the long way around
Watch both camps for a day before deciding

encounters.title: The Sick Child
encounters.description: A child, alone, in a doorway, coughing. No adult visible. A wet, rattling cough. The child is old enough to speak but does not — points to a house and says one word, a name. The house is dark. The child is fevered.

choices.text: Carry the child back to the shelter and the clinic
Search the dark house for the named adult first
Leave medicine and water and continue
Leave — you cannot take on a sick child

encounters.title: The Injured Scavenger
encounters.description: A scavenger at the base of a collapsed building, leg pinned under a fallen beam. Conscious, in pain, asking for water. He has a full pack — he was on his way out when it fell. He says he will share the pack if you free him. He says he will not be angry if you take the pack and leave him the water.

choices.text: Free him and take him at his word — share the pack
Free him but take the full pack as payment
Take the pack and leave him the water, do not free
Free him and leave the pack entirely his

encounters.title: The Roof Access
encounters.description: A stairwell to a roof, the door propped open with a brick. From above, the sound of wind and a faint signal — a radio beacon, automated, still pinging. The stairs are cracked; the fourth step is gone. The beacon might be salvageable. The stairwell might not hold.

choices.text: Climb for the beacon, step over the gap
Call up to see if anyone answers (no one does)
Shore the stairs with the brick and a plank, then climb
Leave it — the beacon is not worth the stairwell

encounters.title: The Cold Storage
encounters.description: A warehouse marked COLD STORAGE, the door sealed with a chain that has been cut and re-chained. Inside, through the gap: frost still on the walls, the hum of a working compressor. Someone is keeping this cold. Someone is keeping something cold. The re-chain is fresh.

choices.text: Cut the fresh chain and enter
Knock and wait — if someone is keeping it, they may answer
Leave a note and a trade offer, do not enter
Leave it — whatever is kept cold is kept cold for a reason

encounters.title: The Hot Sign
encounters.description: A roadside sign, RADIATION HAZARD, the trefoil faded to pink. Your dosimeter ticks faster here — a hot spot, localized, the size of the sign itself. Beneath the sign, a box, locked, the lock rusted. The box is in the hottest part of the hot spot.

choices.text: Rush the box, grab it, retreat — count your seconds
Mark the hot spot and leave the box
Wait for wind to disperse any particulate, then approach
Use a long stick to drag the box out from the hot spot

encounters.title: The Clean Well
encounters.description: A well with a working pump, the water clear and cold. A logbook beside it records six months of tests, all POTABLE, in the same hand — until the last entry, three days ago, which reads ONLY FOR THE LIVING and is in a different hand. The water is still clear. The water is still cold.

choices.text: Drink — the water tests clean and the hand may be mad
Test the water with your own kit before drinking
Fill your canteens and go without drinking
Leave the well — 'only for the living' is a warning

encounters.title: The Whiteout Traveler
encounters.description: In a whiteout, a figure appears, walking the same road, opposite direction. They are not dressed for the cold. They do not seem cold. They ask you the way to a town that you know is gone. They are calm. The snow is heavy. You have minutes before you lose each other.

choices.text: Tell them the town is gone and offer to share the road
Let them go — you cannot save everyone in a whiteout
Give them directions to a town that still stands
Insist on sharing shelter until the whiteout passes

encounters.title: The Flooded Road
encounters.description: The road ahead is under a foot of moving water, brown and fast. A car is stalled mid-road, water up to its windows. The driver is on the roof, waving. A child is in the car. The water is rising. You are on foot. You cannot swim in this.

choices.text: Wade to the car and pass the child to the roof
Throw a line from the bank if you have one
Go for help at the nearest building — you cannot swim this
Watch — you are on foot and the water is too fast for you

encounters.title: The Silent Dogs
encounters.description: A farmstead, dogs in the yard, four of them, and they are silent. Not asleep — watching you, ears forward, tails still. A dog that barks is a warning. A dog that does not bark has been told not to. Someone is in the house. The dogs are waiting for the command.

choices.text: Back away slowly, do not turn, do not run
Call out to the house — announce yourself, hands open
Leave food at the gate and withdraw
Cut through the yard — the dogs may not be commanded yet

encounters.title: The Following Footsteps
encounters.description: On a long straight road, you hear a second set of footsteps behind you, matching your pace. You stop; they stop. You walk; they walk. You do not look back. The footsteps are not loud enough to be a threat and not quiet enough to be imagination. They have been there for a mile.

choices.text: Stop and wait for them to pass or reveal themselves
Speak aloud — offer to share the road
Look back — whatever it is, you want to know
Speed up — let them match or fall behind

encounters.title: The Border Camp
encounters.description: A checkpoint at a territorial border, unmanned but recently manned — the fire is still warm, the barrier is down. A sign: AUTHORIZED PASSAGE ONLY. A logbook records the last three travelers, their business, their direction. The last entry is two hours ago. The guards left in a hurry.

choices.text: Pass quickly while the barrier is down
Sign the logbook and pass — be on the record
Wait for the guards to return and present yourself
Take the logbook — the travelers' business is useful

encounters.title: The Two Factions
encounters.description: A trade meet between two factions you know are hostile. Both have invited you as a neutral witness to the exchange. The goods are on a blanket between them. Neither will touch the blanket first. They are waiting for you to touch it, which will make you the guarantor.

choices.text: Witness only — do not touch the blanket
Touch the blanket to begin the exchange as guarantor
Refuse the role and leave them to it
Propose terms they both can accept without the blanket

encounters.title: The Locked Room
encounters.description: A door, locked from the outside, the key still in the lock. From inside, the sound of water dripping and a clock ticking. The key turns easily — the lock is not stuck. Someone locked this room from the outside and left the key. Someone wanted it opened.

choices.text: Turn the key and open the door
Knock first — if someone is inside, let them speak
Leave the key and the door — it is not your room
Take the key and go — open it later, with others

encounters.title: The Two Graves
encounters.description: Two fresh graves, side by side, marked with the same name on both — the same first name, the same date, different last names. A single shovel, clean, leaning on a tree. The dirt is fresh. The digger is not here. The names are the names of two people, or one person twice, or a mistake.

choices.text: Dig one up to settle the question
Leave something on both and go
Wait for the digger to return and ask
Mark the site on your map and leave it be

encounters.title: The Beggars at the Gate
encounters.description: Three people at the shelter gate, asking for food. They are not sick, not injured, just hungry. You have food for your own, counted to the day. The gate guard looks to you. The three are calm. They will go if turned away. They will remember.

choices.text: Share one meal from the counted stores
Turn them away — the count is the count
Offer food for a day's work at the shelter
Direct them to a settlement with more

encounters.title: The Thief Child
encounters.description: A child, caught stealing from your packs — a handful of dried fruit, already eaten. The child is thin. The child is crying. The child is not yours and not of your shelter. The guard has hold of the child's arm. The child's parent, if there is one, is not here.

choices.text: Feed the child and release them with a warning
Find the parent and return the child
Punish as a deterrent — the stores are the stores
Take the child into the shelter

encounters.title: The Library Cache
encounters.description: A public library, the shelves mostly bare, but one section — geology — is intact, and behind the geology books, a cache: water, a blanket, a notebook. The notebook is a log of who has sheltered here and for how long. The last entry is a week ago. The cache is for travelers. The cache is trusted.

choices.text: Use the cache and replenish what you can
Take only the water and sign the notebook
Add to the cache and take nothing
Take the cache — it is unguarded

encounters.title: The Greenhouse Keeper
encounters.description: A greenhouse, mostly glass gone, but one corner still glazed and warm. Inside, a woman tending a single row of seedlings. She has a shotgun, leaned, not aimed. She says she will trade seedlings for salt. She says she will not trade the shotgun. She has been here alone for months.

choices.text: Trade salt for seedlings
Offer a day's labor for the seedlings and her company
Take the seedlings by force
Leave and report the greenhouse to the shelter

encounters.title: The Dead Radio Operator
encounters.description: A relay station, the operator dead at the desk, the headphones still on. The equipment is still running. The last log entry is from this morning — he was alive hours ago. The broadcast is still transmitting, automated now. He died with the headphones on and no one turned it off.

choices.text: Turn off the broadcast and bury the operator
Keep the broadcast running — it may guide others
Take the headphones and the logbook
Send a message on the working equipment, then decide

encounters.title: The Ice Fishermen
encounters.description: Two figures on a frozen lake, ice fishing, a hole cut, lines in the water. They have fish — three, on the ice, frozen. They wave. The ice is black where they are. The ice is white near the shore. They are on the black. They do not seem to know, or do not care.

choices.text: Walk out and warn them — the black is the deep
Call to them from the shore — do not go on the black
Wait for them to come to shore, then trade for the fish
Watch — if they fall, you cannot help them anyway

encounters.title: The Quarantine Sign
encounters.description: A house with a QUARANTINE sign, painted on a sheet, hung in the window. The sign is old. From inside, a child's voice, singing, faintly. The singing is cheerful. The sign says QUARANTINE. The singing says otherwise. The door is unlocked.

choices.text: Enter — the sign is old and the singing is alive
Call through the door — do not enter
Leave supplies at the door and go
Report the house to the nearest clinic and leave

encounters.title: The Last Train
encounters.description: A train, stopped on the track, doors open, no one aboard. The driver's cab is empty. The schedule board shows a destination that is a town you know is flooded. The train has power — the lights are on. The train is going nowhere. The track ahead is underwater.

choices.text: Search the train for supplies
Take the battery from the driver's cab
Leave a note in the cab and go
Watch the track — a train with power may have an owner
